answer: Behavior fingerprints stop bulk fakes. Each identity locks 70 credits, escrows a knoll-route fingerprint. It reruns the route each epoch, filing a cipher-signed log of plume readings; an auditor checks it against the escrow, and a mismatch or shared fingerprint burns the bond. Filing k costs 40+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 and lock 70,000 vs a 40,000 pool; no rented-fingerprint ring survives. One honest run costs 40 and keeps its bond.
